TL;DR

Illustration Studio, in short.

1The problem

A lending app is full of states, and each one needs a picture. With six PMs and one designer, 10 to 15 state graphics a month waited in my queue, and PMs waited days for each.

2What I built

A studio where PMs choose instead of draw. Every graphic is the same five layers with rules, coloured from the Design Kit, and exported as SVG, Lottie and PNG in every size and mode.

3What changed

PMs made 40+ graphics themselves in the first month. A state graphic went from a day of my design work to 10 minutes, made by the PM who needs it, and every graphic ships with dark mode and motion.

Try it · or just describe it

What I'd do differently. Test at the size people see, from day one. My worst bugs, accents too small to notice, only showed up at real phone size.

Next in the system: Design Kit →
01The tension

Every state screen was a small design project.

A lending app is full of states: approved, pending, failed, nothing here yet, allow access, verify your KYC. Each one needs a picture. With six PMs and one designer, every one of them waited in my queue: 10 to 15 new state graphics a month, each drawn from scratch or adapted from stock. PMs waited days for a picture, and every one pulled me off the problem the screen was meant to solve.

  • SlowA day of design work each, after 2 to 3 days in the queue.
  • InconsistentEvery product area drifted into its own style.
  • No dark modeEvery graphic was drawn for light screens only.
  • No motionLottie took too long, so it was usually skipped.
02The insight

Illustrations are a system, not artwork.

Pull any state graphic apart and it's the same five layers. If those layers follow rules, the graphic can be generated instead of drawn.

03The build

I built the studio in a week, with Claude.

Pick an object, a status badge, a style, a background, accents and motion. The studio draws it in Rupyy's theme and exports SVG for the web, Lottie for the app and PNG for docs, in every size and mode at once.

Any object, any state

48 objects and 6 states give 288 starting points before a single setting changes. Below, six of each, generated, not drawn.

Or just describe it

Type the screen in plain words. Claude sets up the graphic inside the studio's rules and theme. When nothing in the library fits, it draws a new object in the house style and saves it as a draft for review.

It talks to the other two when it needs to

One system
  • Design KitGives the palette; takes approved graphics back as parts.
  • Journey StudioScreens name a graphic, so prototypes and the app match.

I design the system; Claude builds it. I set the five layers, the rules and the motion; Claude writes the code and powers Describe, inside those rules.

04The guardrails

Guardrails let PMs move fast safely.

Self-serve only works if nobody can break the brand by accident. So the studio checks every graphic as it's made, and suggests a one-click fix when something's off.

Decision 1A generator, not an illustration library

Instead ofcommissioning a set or buying stock

Build rules. New states keep coming; a generator covers every size, mode and motion in one style.

Decision 2AI inside the rules, not around them

Describe changes the studio's own settings, never pixels. New objects start as drafts until someone approves them.

Decision 3No badge colour picker

A badge's colour is its meaning. Three styles instead. Neutral is kept for badges with no status, like a shield, and the studio warns if a tick or cross loses its colour.

Try it: break the brand
Badge
Badge style

Suggestions

Set a status badge to Neutral and watch the studio push back. Then try Shield.

What I got wrong first

My first accents looked wrong. My own review notes said it plainly: “similar-looking weird shapes, not randomised enough.” Random placement clumped, and small shapes vanished on a phone.

So I replaced luck with rules: equal slices, balanced weight, a minimum size. Then I rendered one graphic in all 64,800 combinations of its settings. That found 13 more issues no single screenshot showed, and every fix became a check the studio runs by itself.

Accents were too small to see on a phone. Now nothing goes under 6 px on screen.

05The impact

Shipped. From a design ticket to ten minutes.

The studio is in production and the whole product team uses it. Six PMs make their own state graphics, design approves them, and developers take SVG and Lottie straight from the kit.

What I'd do differently

Test at the size people see, from day one. My worst bugs, accents too small to notice, only showed up at real phone size. I'd also bring a developer in on day one, to prove the Lottie hand-off end to end before growing the library.
